After a long offseason and a full slate of Spring Training games, Opening Day is when baseball officially returns.. For fans, it’s the first chance to see new rosters in action, celebrate the return of game-day traditions and be there for one of the most anticipated days of the season.In 2026, the season gets started on March 25, when the New York Yankees and San Francisco Giants open things up at Oracle Park in San Francisco. Then on March 26, the other 28 teams will take the field for their first game of the year, turning Opening Day into a league-wide celebration. Whether you’re heading out for the atmosphere or the traditions, Opening Day is one of the best times all season to catch an MLB game live.Why is MLB Opening Day such a big deal?Opening Day has a special place in baseball because it signals a fresh start for every team and fanbase. It’s often treated like a celebration, with pregame ceremonies, first pitches, special giveaways, and packed stadiums creating a playoff-like atmosphere.Are MLB Opening Day tickets more expensive than other regular-season tickets?They can be. Opening Day is one of the most in-demand regular-season games of the year, so prices are often higher than for a typical game. Pricing depends on the matchup, ballpark, seat location, and demand. On SeatGeek, you can track prices over time and use tools like Deal Score and interactive seat maps to spot the best values as they appear, so you know when it’s a good time to buy.When should I buy MLB Opening Day tickets?Earlier is usually better. Because Opening Day is a marquee event, popular sections can sell quickly, especially for rivalry games, home openers and teams with strong fan demand.Is MLB Opening Day the same as a home opener?Not necessarily. A team’s Opening Day game is its first regular-season game, but its home opener is its first game played at home. Some teams begin the season on the road and host their home opener later.When is MLB Opening Day this year?For the 2026 season, MLB opens with Yankees vs. Giants on Wednesday, March 25, 2026, with a bigger Opening Day slate taking place on Thursday, March 26, 2026 and other teams starting their season on Friday, March 27, 2026.SeatGeek: Official Ticket Marketplace of MLB SeatGeek is the Official Ticket Marketplace for all MLB teams, including your MLB Opening Day! MLB Opening Day games, like most Major League Baseball (MLB) games, typically last around 2 hours and 36 minutes. This average duration has been consistent across the league since the implementation of the pitch clock in 2023, which significantly reduced game times from previous years.While the average game lasts 2 hours and 36 minutes, actual MLB Opening Day game durations can vary. Factors such as extra innings, high-scoring games, or frequent pitching changes can extend the length of a MLB Opening Day game. Conversely, games with efficient pitching and quick innings may conclude in less time.Planning for a 3-hour window is typically a safe bet for a MLB Opening Day game!What happens if a MLB Opening Day game is rained out?
